editions.title: Nine straight wins, a late-goal habit and PSV at the Bernabéu
editions.dek: Madrid came from behind to beat Celta for a ninth straight win and now host PSV, top of the Eredivisie but 24th in the Champions League, with Vinicius back in the XI.

editions.title: Two down in seven minutes, three goals in ten: how Barça turned Villarreal around
editions.dek: Barça came from 0-2 down to beat Villarreal 3-2 and stay three points clear, but go to Sabah without Lamine Yamal and may lose Fermín for two games.

editions.title: Simeone reaches 345 and Atlético find their edge again
editions.dek: Atlético’s 3-0 win at Getafe made Diego Simeone LaLiga’s winningest coach, but a side 23rd in the Champions League must now beat Viking.

editions.title: Four contracts in three days: Arsenal lock down the champions
editions.dek: Arsenal agreed four new contracts in three days as Andrea Berta locked down the spine of the title-winning squad, with Calafiori next in line.

editions.title: Eight minutes into the Pochettino era, United's season found a new low
editions.dek: Mauricio Pochettino's first game as Manchester United head coach ended 4-0 at Anfield after an eighth-minute red card, leaving United 19th with 8 points.

editions.title: Four without a win, and De Bruyne is coming back
editions.dek: City drew with Fulham for a fourth league game without a win, and now host a depleted Napoli and Kevin De Bruyne before a trip to leaders Arsenal.

editions.title: Wirtz and Ngumoha run riot as Liverpool take Pochettino's United apart
editions.dek: Liverpool beat ten-man Manchester United 4-0 at Anfield as Wirtz and Ngumoha ran riot, a statement win before Wednesday's Champions League trip to Club Brugge.

editions.title: Fragile at the Bridge: Leeds rout lays bare what Alonso's Chelsea lack
editions.dek: Leeds won 4-1 at Stamford Bridge, exposing a fragile Chelsea side as Xabi Alonso keeps the owners' backing before Friday's trip to Nottingham Forest.

editions.title: Pochettino Walks Into The Oldest Fight In England
editions.dek: Mauricio Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United for the first time at Anfield on Sunday, four days into the job with his club in the relegation zone.

editions.title: Venezia at home, and no more room for drift
editions.dek: Juventus return from the break seventh and 11 points off the top, with Venezia at home, a long injury list easing and Conte openly talking about a comeback.

editions.title: Lautaro and Thuram return as Inter restart the chase in Bergamo
editions.dek: Lautaro Martinez and Marcus Thuram are back in training as second-placed Inter visit Atalanta on Sunday, a point behind Lazio, with Stuttgart three days later.

editions.title: Douvikas alone: Como's striker crisis meets four games in 12 days
editions.dek: A new tibia setback for Moise Kean leaves Tasos Douvikas as the only fit Como striker for four home games in 12 days, starting with Cagliari on Saturday and AEK Athens on Tuesday.

editions.title: Five points back, three games in nine days: Amorim's Milan restart the chase
editions.dek: Fourth and five points off the top, Amorim's Milan resume against Frosinone at San Siro before a pivotal Europa League trip to Olympiacos.

editions.title: Eleven straight wins, and the injured stars are almost back
editions.dek: PSG return from the international break at Nice chasing a 12th straight win, with Dembélé, Marquinhos and Nuno Mendes close to fitness and Doué a doubt.

editions.title: Kompany comes home: Bayern's coach returns for Köln, and the unbeaten interregnum ends
editions.dek: Vincent Kompany returns for Friday's game with Koln after his October collapse, inheriting an unbeaten Bayern side level on points with Dortmund and short of Neuer and Davies.

editions.title: Vinícius returns with five goals, and Mourinho has a choice to make
editions.dek: Vinicius returns from the break with five Brazil goals, Tchouameni is a doubt and Madrid face three home games in eight days, starting with Celta Vigo.

editions.title: A costly break: Cubarsí a doubt as Barça face seven games in 21 days
editions.dek: Barça return from the international break with Cubarsí a doubt, Raphinha chastened and seven games in 21 days, starting with Villarreal at Spotify Camp Nou on Sunday.

editions.title: Atlético's November gauntlet starts at Getafe, with history in reach and bodies short
editions.dek: Atlético come out of the international break short of Lookman, Pubill and Cuti Romero, with Simeone one win from a La Liga record and four games in eleven days ahead.

editions.title: Arsenal Spend the Break Locking the Doors
editions.dek: Declan Rice has agreed a new five-year Arsenal deal to 2031, with David Raya, Jurrien Timber and Piero Hincapie close behind, turning a quiet international break into Arsenal's biggest week of business.

editions.title: Pochettino takes over a club in the bottom three
editions.dek: Manchester United sacked Michael Carrick with the team 18th and hired Mauricio Pochettino, who starts on November 18 and makes his debut at Anfield on November 22.

editions.title: Eight days that will define Maresca's autumn
editions.dek: City return from the break with Fulham, Napoli and leaders Arsenal in eight days, needing to fix a leaky defence while Guéhi is a doubt and an appeal date looms.

editions.title: Pochettino's United arrive at Anfield as Liverpool count the cost of the break
editions.dek: Liverpool return from the international break to face Pochettino's first Manchester United side at Anfield, with Van Dijk, Szoboszlai, Araujo and Gravenberch all fitness questions.

editions.title: Ten games in, Alonso's Chelsea need Leeds to be a turning point
editions.dek: Fifth and two points off the top four, Chelsea return from the break against Leeds with João Pedro doubtful and questions to answer after the defeat at Sunderland.

editions.title: Pochettino swaps the USMNT for a United rescue mission
editions.dek: Manchester United sack Michael Carrick and hire USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino, who starts on 18 November and goes to Anfield four days later.

editions.title: Six points off fourth, and a fortnight to fix it
editions.dek: Juventus drew 2-2 at Fiorentina to sit seventh, six points off fourth, as Spalletti faces growing scrutiny heading into the international break and a home game with Venezia.

editions.title: Inter give Como the ball and take the points
editions.dek: Inter beat Como 2-0 with only 43 percent of the ball to go into the international break a point behind Lazio, with Sarri's injury-hit Atalanta up next.

editions.title: Back to earth at San Siro: what Inter exposed, and what the break must fix
editions.dek: Four days after a record 9-1 at Lens, Como lost 2-0 at Inter, ending a six-game winning run and dropping to fifth before the November break.

editions.title: Amorim's split season: a Serie A contender, a Europa League emergency
editions.dek: Milan sit fourth on 24 points after winning at Genoa, but a 2-0 home loss to Ferencvaros leaves them 28th in the Europa League and Amorim admitting the squad is not ready.

editions.title: Eleven straight wins, and PSG did it without their stars
editions.dek: PSG reach the international break on an 11-match winning run built without Kvaratskhelia, Dembélé and Marquinhos, and will not buy a winter replacement for the Georgian.

editions.title: Two tight wins, 21 points and the closest title race in years
editions.dek: Dortmund beat Real Betis and Elversberg 2-1 to stay level with Bayern on 21 points, but fatigue and injuries to Guirassy and Chukwuemeka cloud the international break.

editions.title: Kane signs on to 2029 as Bayern lead the table into a bruising break
editions.dek: Harry Kane extends to 2029 at a reported club-record salary while Bayern lead the Bundesliga on goal difference without Kompany, Neuer, Musiala and Saibari.

editions.title: Five Clear, Seven Clean Sheets, One Winger Missing
editions.dek: Arsenal reach the last international break of the year top of the Premier League on 27 points, five clear, with the meanest defence in the division and Bukayo Saka still weeks away.

editions.title: Eight in a row, and Mourinho's Madrid have found a shape
editions.dek: Real Madrid head into the November break on an eight-game winning run, three points behind Barcelona, with Diomande's rise and Vinicius's slump the key questions.

editions.title: Fermín's double at the Metropolitano sends Barça into the break three points clear
editions.dek: Fermín scored twice in his 100th La Liga game as Barcelona came from behind to win 2-1 at Atlético and go into the break three points clear.

editions.title: Two Nights at the Metropolitano, One Hard Lesson
editions.dek: Back-to-back home defeats to Bayern and Barcelona ended a seven-game league winning run and exposed the gap Simeone admits still exists.

editions.title: Carrick's reprieve runs into the international break
editions.dek: United go into the international break 18th after a 4-4 draw with Villa, and the board will reassess Michael Carrick's position before the trip to Liverpool.

editions.title: Seven up, three down: what has gone wrong for Maresca's City
editions.dek: Seven straight wins have turned into three defeats as Forest beat City 3-1, exposing structural flaws and new defensive injuries before a brutal run of fixtures.

editions.title: Liverpool find an answer at Selhurst, but the set-piece leak still stings
editions.dek: After losing to Arsenal and Fenerbahce, Liverpool won 3-1 at Crystal Palace to sit fourth, nine points behind Arsenal, with set-piece defending still their biggest worry.

editions.title: No striker, no spark: Chelsea stall at the Stadium of Light
editions.dek: Sunderland's 1-0 win sent Chelsea into the international break fifth and 11 points behind Arsenal, with the absence of João Pedro badly felt.

editions.title: Five weeks, two wet weekends, and the first playoff night PayPal Park has ever had
editions.dek: The Valkyries lifted a title at Chase Center, San Jose hosts its first home playoff match, rain lands on two of the next four weekends, and the holiday markets begin.

editions.title: Three clubs, three points, and Atletico host Barcelona on Sunday
editions.dek: La Liga's top three are separated by three points, and Atletico Madrid can go top on Sunday by beating a Barcelona side travelling without the injured Rodri.

editions.title: Ten days on a knife edge: Spalletti's Juventus fight for air
editions.dek: After a retreat and a rare speech from the chief executive, Juventus beat Napoli and AZ Alkmaar in five days, but a thin squad and a wary club keep Spalletti on edge.

editions.title: Stung by the derby, revived in Rotterdam: Inter face Como's test
editions.dek: After a first league defeat in the derby, Inter rebuilt with a 3-0 win in Rotterdam and now host high-flying Como in a Serie A top-four clash on Sunday.

editions.title: Nine at Bollaert: Como rewrite the Champions League record book
editions.dek: Como's 9-1 win at Lens equalled the Champions League record winning margin and set an Italian scoring mark, with a trip to Inter at San Siro up next.

editions.title: After the derby, the night that decides Milan's European autumn
editions.dek: Milan beat Inter 3-1 to climb to fifth in Serie A, but sit 24th in the Europa League and must beat unbeaten Ferencváros tonight at San Siro.

editions.title: Six goals, ten wins, no Dembélé: PSG's understudies run riot in Villarreal
editions.dek: Without Dembélé, Kvaratskhelia and Marquinhos, PSG crushed Villarreal 6-0 for a record 20 goals in four Champions League games and a tenth straight win.

editions.title: The back four that held Munich now meets Betis and their perfect record
editions.dek: Dortmund drew 2-2 at Bayern after Niko Kovac switched to a back four, and now host unbeaten Real Betis in the Champions League tonight.

editions.title: In Kompany's absence, Bayern find another gear
editions.dek: Interim coach Aaron Danks has kept an injury-hit Bayern unbeaten in four games without Vincent Kompany, capped by a 2-0 win at Atlético Madrid.

editions.title: Mourinho's Madrid take a six-game charge to Athens
editions.dek: Real Madrid travel to AEK Athens on a six-game winning run, with Mourinho rotating, Güler and Tchouaméni rested and Vinícius back for Europe.

editions.title: Villa at the Camp Nou: a patched-up Barça defence meets Europe's form side
editions.dek: Barça host Aston Villa, perfect in Europe, tonight with four defenders injured, then travel to Atlético for first against second in LaLiga on Sunday.

editions.title: Bayern come to the Metropolitano with Atlético's midfield stretched thin
editions.dek: Atlético host Bayern Munich without Romero, Hjulmand and Cardoso, five days before Barcelona visit with first place in La Liga on the line.

editions.title: Fourteen Years, One Goal, And A Defensive Masterclass At Anfield
editions.dek: Arsenal won 1-0 at Anfield for the first time in 14 years, go three points clear at the top, and get William Saliba back for Prague.

editions.title: Carrick's Roma reckoning: one night to change the story
editions.dek: Michael Carrick faces Roma at Old Trafford with United 17th, winless in nine and his position set to be assessed at the international break.

editions.title: Maresca's first real test: two defeats, a lost lead and a trip to Leipzig
editions.dek: After losses at Villa and at home to Brighton, City have dropped to second behind Arsenal, and Enzo Maresca must fix a leaky defence before facing RB Leipzig.

editions.title: No shot on target, no answer: Arsenal expose Liverpool's Anfield problem
editions.dek: Arsenal won 1-0 at Anfield after an Alisson error, Liverpool failed to register a shot on target, and a home attack with four league goals in five games now heads to Istanbul.

editions.title: Lavia, Rogers and a rare clean sheet: how Alonso steadied a lurching week
editions.dek: Chelsea beat ten-man Manchester United 2-0 after a week of a Spurs defeat and a Carabao Cup shootout exit, with Lavia and Rogers leading the way before a trip to Sunderland.

editions.title: Der Klassiker arrives level, and without the man who built Bayern's season
editions.dek: Bayern and Dortmund meet level on points and both unbeaten in a Klassiker Vincent Kompany will watch from home, with Aaron Danks in the dugout.

editions.title: Kane's Crown, and the Klassiker That Follows
editions.dek: Harry Kane collected the Ballon d'Or in London on Monday and now walks into a first-against-second Klassiker at the Allianz Arena with Bayern's head coach in hospital.

editions.title: Anfield, Without Him
editions.dek: Arsenal go to Anfield on Sunday level on points with Manchester City but without Bukayo Saka, who faces weeks out with a quad injury.

editions.title: Five weeks, three holidays, and one deadline this Saturday
editions.dek: Day of the Dead fills the Mission, nine Warriors home dates land at Chase Center, and Dickens Fair Early Bird pricing ends October 31.

editions.title: Mourinho Walks Back Into the Camp Nou
editions.dek: Jose Mourinho takes Real Madrid back to the Camp Nou on Sunday six points adrift of an unbeaten Barcelona and without Vinicius Junior.

editions.title: Back to Munich, Carrying a Different Kind of Problem
editions.dek: Arsenal go to the Allianz Arena as English champions with a perfect Champions League record and a scoring problem nobody has solved yet.

editions.title: The champions of Europe walk into the one place nobody is losing
editions.dek: Paris Saint-Germain, winners of the last two Champions Leagues, visit an unbeaten Manchester City on a matchday that has already produced 32 goals in nine games.

editions.title: A new contract, two wins in four days, and the answer last month's defeat demanded
editions.dek: Arsenal followed Mikel Arteta's new contract to 2030 with a comeback win over Leeds and a 3-0 Champions League rout of Lille, in a week that ended with the death of Ken Friar.

editions.title: Five weeks, and a Finals in our own building
editions.dek: The Valkyries host the first WNBA Finals games ever played in San Francisco, the Warriors open at home, and autumn festivals run from Half Moon Bay to Sonoma.

editions.title: The clock started at 7pm on Thursday
editions.dek: Manchester City lodged their appeal against the guilty verdict at 7pm on 1 October, starting a twelve-week clock that will decide when, and how hard, any punishment lands.

editions.title: Twenty-one days to fix the thing nobody has fixed
editions.dek: Arsenal return from a three week international break second in the table with eight goals in five games and the sharpest question of their season still unanswered.

editions.title: Guilty: the verdict that rewrites nine seasons of English football
editions.dek: An independent commission found Manchester City guilty of serious financial breaches across nine seasons, and the sanction is still to come.

editions.title: No match, no peace: Arteta signs up for four more years
editions.dek: With no Arsenal men's match all week, Mikel Arteta agreed a reported four-year deal and Manchester City were found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules.

editions.title: Five weeks of the real San Francisco summer, ending on a Saturday Halloween
editions.dek: A catch-up edition for five weeks of fall: Fleet Week, Hardly Strictly, Valkyries playoff nights, pumpkins on the coast and a Halloween weekend.

editions.title: Football's Cold War Reaches the Ballot Box
editions.dek: UEFA and FIFA are at war over who owns the World Cup, and this week the fight moved openly into the 2027 election campaign.

editions.title: Arteta Gets His Deal. His Champions Get a Warning.
editions.dek: Arsenal and Mikel Arteta have agreed a new long-term contract, the BBC reports, three days after Brighton beat the champions 3-0 on the south coast.

editions.title: The Great Reshuffle Meets Its First Reckoning
editions.dek: Europe's great managerial reshuffle faces its first verdicts as Maresca's Manchester City go four from four and Mourinho's Real Madrid chase Barcelona.

editions.title: The one trophy that keeps getting away
editions.dek: Arsenal begin the Carabao Cup at Ipswich six months after losing its final, unbeaten in six and missing half a back four.

editions.title: Five weeks from the Moon Festival to the pumpkin fields
editions.dek: A catch-up edition for mid-September to mid-October: Portola, Folsom, Hardly Strictly, Fleet Week, the Giants' last homestand and the Valkyries' run-in.

editions.title: Europe Reopens on a Map Nobody Recognises
editions.dek: The Champions League league phase opens on a redrawn map of Europe, with Mourinho at Real Madrid, Maresca at City and the holders PSG 14th in France.

editions.title: Naples, a grounded plane and a back four held together by faith
editions.dek: Arsenal open their Champions League campaign at Napoli on Wednesday with William Saliba out, Ezri Konsa two games into his Arsenal career and Martin Odegaard in the form of his life.

editions.title: The night the window broke its own record, then broke its word
editions.dek: A record 3.46 billion pound Premier League window closed with Enzo Fernandez joining Manchester City for 125m and two agreed deals collapsing after the buzzer.

editions.title: Arsenal Sell the Summer and Back What They Already Have
editions.dek: Arsenal close the window having sold Gabriel Jesus and Gabriel Martinelli, missed out on Malick Fofana and loaned Ethan Nwaneri to Dortmund, all while unbeaten and yet to concede.

editions.title: Five weeks, and the best free weekend of the year at the end of them
editions.dek: Labor Day weekend opens a five-week run that ends with Hardly Strictly free in the park, plus Portola, Folsom and the Giants' last homestand.

editions.title: Six days left, and the money has not stopped moving
editions.dek: Six days from the September 1 deadline, a World Cup summer has pushed Europe's most expensive week into the middle of the season.

editions.title: Six Days to Remake a Forward Line
editions.dek: Arsenal open the title defence with two 3-0 wins and six days left to remake a forward line, with Gabriel Martinelli close to a record Saudi exit.

editions.title: Ten New Voices, One Compressed Summer
editions.dek: Europe restarts 33 days after the World Cup with ten new Premier League managers, Rodri sold to Barcelona and Pep Guardiola gone after a decade.

editions.title: Champions Again, and Already One Defender Short
editions.dek: Arsenal begin their Premier League title defence against Coventry on Friday, three days after a 3-0 Community Shield win and with the centre-back department still unfixed.

editions.title: Festival season just ended and the city is better for it
editions.dek: Outside Lands packed up ten days ago and Stern Grove closed with Al Green yesterday afternoon.
